newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat mixed amid crop uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat mixed amid crop uncertainty.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures were narrowly mixed at midsession amid uncertainty about U.S. spring wheat production prospects, traders said.

"It's very quiet and not much paper. I think the spring crop is better than what the government says but they'll (crop scouts) be out there this week and I think they'll find more bushels," a trader said.
USDA's current estimate for the 1997 U.S. spring wheat crop stands at 569 million bushels, below industry expectations for 634 million.
A tour this week of the U.S. spring wheat region was expected to report a lack of uniformity of yield potential plus some disease problems.
"There's a pretty big variety across the state," said Pat Berglund, director of the Northern Crops Institute referring to the expectations for North Dakota's spring wheat production.
Traders said the wheat markets in Minneapolis, Kansas City and Chicago were underpinned earlier by a surge in corn and soybean futures.

Also, there may have been some support from news Egypt over the weekend bought at least 200,000 tonnes U.S. wheat as well as on expectations Pakistan this week will buy wheat from the U.S. But many traders said the Egyptian and Pakistani business was expected which limited the bullish effect of the deals.
At 1117 CDT, MGE spring wheat was one cent lower to one cent higher, with September up 1/2 at $3.85-1/2 per bushel.
